one_line_contribution: That the harm from retrieved-experience memory in a ReAct agent is mediated by premature termination of evidence gathering — outcome-bearing items shorten the search — such that a content-free, programmatically enforced evidence floor repairs it while a GEPA-searched instruction cannot.
closest_prior_work: Two threats. (a) Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067, which the proposal correctly identifies and correctly does not try to re-own; after crediting it, the residual novelty is a mediator variable and an intervention, not a phenomenon. (b) The one the proposal never mentions and that I think is more damaging: the RAG knowledge-conflict / context-over-reliance literature. The finding that a model presented with a plausible answer in its context adopts it and stops reasoning, that entity-substituted corpora make the model return the context-consistent stale value, and that 'does the supporting evidence appear in the retrieved context' (sufficient-context style labelling) predicts unfaithful answering, are all established there on non-agentic RAG. Analysis 5 is an entity-substitution conflict probe with 'memory' in place of 'retrieved passage'; prediction 2 restates over-reliance; prediction 8 restates the known confidence miscalibration under conflicting context. The proposal's genuine delta over that literature is that the shortcut manifests as *fewer tool calls* rather than as a wrong answer at fixed context — real, but narrower than the abstract claims. arXiv:2604.27003's procedural-beats-trajectory result further pre-empts M2>M3 directionally, as the proposal concedes.
strongest_objection: Prediction 6 — the headline 'instruction optimization cannot own this' — is close to definitionally true as operationalized, and where it is not definitional it is confounded. M1+Fh is a harness that *rejects* the answer and *forces* up to three additional tool calls; G1 and M1+Fs are text that *asks* for the same behaviour. Any hard constraint beats any soft request in a small open-weight model, on any pathology, with or without memory; a 'GEPA writes verification language and compliance does not move' result is an instruction-following result about Qwen2.5-14B, not a division-of-labour result about memory-induced shortcutting. The confound is concrete and uncontrolled: Fh grants extra call budget beyond the shared step limit, G1 does not, and M6 gives the budget control only to M1 — there is no G1+budget or M1+Fs+budget arm, so part of the floor's advantage over G1 is purchased affordance rather than enforcement-versus-instruction. Second, independent objection: the interaction in Analysis 2 compares floor efficacy on non-comparable error populations. M1's breaks are, by selection, instances M0 already solved — shallow, recoverable errors. M0's errors include genuinely hard multi-hop failures the floor cannot fix at any call budget. So (M1−M1+Fh) > (M0−M0+Fh) is the expected result from error composition and headroom alone, with no memory-specific mechanism. Third, prediction 1 conditions on a collider: break/fix subsets are defined by the M1-vs-M0 outcome, then compared on trajectory length. Episodes that terminate early are more likely to be wrong under M0 too, so 'broken instances have shorter trajectories' is partly guaranteed by the selection rule and is reported with no within-M0 length-vs-correctness null.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Make the repair ladder affordance-matched: run G1 and M1+Fs with the same +3-call allowance the floor consumes, and — the arm that would make (iii) a real claim — give GEPA the *same programmatic hook* the floor uses (optimizer writes the sufficiency criterion, harness enforces it). If optimizer-authored enforcement matches Fh, the claim is 'the instruction slot cannot enforce', which is honest and modest; if it does not, the claim is about search, not about slots. (2) Cross the floor with the content arms (M2+Fh, M3+Fh, M4+Fh). As written the paper has a content half and a control-flow half that never meet; M3+Fh is the single most informative cell, because it asks whether enforcement neutralizes the maximally shortcutting content. (3) Report the M0-only correlation between trajectory length and correctness as the null expectation for prediction 1, and re-derive the mediation against it. (4) Stratify the M0+Fh comparison by matched instance difficulty, or use M4+Fh rather than M0+Fh as the reference for the interaction, so the contrast is between error populations of comparable recoverability. (5) Report GEPA at more than one search seed and more than 400 rollouts, since the load-bearing result is a negative about a stochastic search. (6) Drop or re-power prediction 4's fix-retention threshold: at a 4% precheck floor, 'M2 retains ≥70% of M1's fixes' is a proportion over ~20 instances and cannot be estimated to anything like that resolution.
missing_baseline: Demonstration-slot optimization. The division-of-labour ladder has exactly two rungs — instruction search (G1) and control flow (Fh) — plus a fixed k=3. The track's own framing puts the memory/demonstration slot in play, and the obvious competitor is optimizing *what gets injected*: MIPRO-style demonstration selection over the frozen bank, or a per-instance calibrated injection budget that admits items only when retrieval-conflict is low. If selecting better items, or admitting fewer of them adaptively, matches the floor's break reduction while keeping fixes, then the repair does belong to a prompt-optimization surface after all and prediction (iii) is refuted by an arm the plan never runs. A reviewer will also demand G1+Fh (are they redundant or additive?) and a late-injection control, where memory is shown only after the agent has gathered evidence, which tests the ordering account of truncation without any enforcement machinery.
preprint_collision: Better than most: it names a real closest work, states an explicit partial collision on the phenomenon, admits that a prior draft contained a dozen unverifiable forward-dated IDs, and states the ICLR/NeurIPS portal gap. That honesty is credited. But it is still weak as evidence of novelty. No queries, dates, venues, or search surfaces are reported, so the search is unauditable. Having disclosed that an earlier draft fabricated IDs, the section then rests on six IDs (2604.27003, 2605.24941, 2608.02508, 2605.18930, 2512.16962, 2607.06595) that I cannot verify and whose fabrication risk the proposal itself has established; the honest disclosure ironically lowers my confidence in the surviving citations rather than raising it. More substantively, the search is aimed only at agent-memory work and misses the two literatures most likely to contain the result: (a) RAG knowledge-conflict and context-over-reliance, where entity-substituted corpora, context-consistent stale answers, and confidence miscalibration under conflicting evidence are established — Analysis 5 is that paradigm rebadged, and it is cited nowhere; (b) sufficient-context / attribution work in RAG, which supplies the exact evidence-sufficiency label the mediation model depends on; (c) deep-research and search-agent work on under-searching and test-time search-depth scaling, which the proposal waves off as 'early exit as a desired efficiency behaviour' — that is not the same as having searched for papers that force additional retrieval before answering and measure the accuracy gain. I do not believe there is a single preprint making this exact mediated claim about agentic memory, so this is not a fatal collision; but the unsearched neighbouring literature means the novelty on the mechanism is smaller than claimed, and the collision check does not establish otherwise.
